shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Three uniformly-efficient per-level sizes (126/190/254) and level counts are bought from a 146,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Mountain mass renders through every level down to the first solid floor, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §0 handover; §1-19 architecture; §20 compat; §21-29 bug records; §30 utility networks. Keep every ⚠ - each cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~73 files, ~21,300 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text.

# 0. START HERE

**What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

**Two things just changed and neither is verified in play.** §2 (the whole tier ladder + a 24% budget cut) and §30a (the power gutter clamp). Both compile. The renderer is CLOSED - the user called visuality done.

**The single most important open risk (unchanged).** §29's depth cut ships ON having been judged only by eye. **If any performance report arrives on a mountainous map, throw `MassDepthCutEnabled` first.**

**How to test.** `run_test_cycle`, then read the profile's TILE and PLAN lines BEFORE looking at anything else. For §30 you need the host mod active - use `companionMods`.

---

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather, settings VERIFIED. **190x5 VERIFIED (#237-#240) but that plan NO LONGER EXISTS - 190 now caps at 4 levels.**
**✅ §24b ✅ §24c ✅ §27 ✅ §28 ✅ §29 accepted on look (#260).**
**🔧 §25 FIXED, UNVERIFIED** (fog-on-reload + doubled/inverted stairs). Needs the reporter's save.
**🔧 §2 NEW LADDER, UNVERIFIED** - 126/190/254 at 146,000. Every previously measured run used the OLD ladder.
**🔧 §30a BUILT, UNVERIFIED** (power gutter leak - `ABPowerBandScope.cs`, guard `ABGuard.Utilities`).
**🚧 §30b-e DESIGNED, NOT BUILT.** Gates resolved, texture tooling shipped, no defs written.

**PUBLISHED-BUILD BUGS.** 1-11 FIXED (§21-29). **12. Power leaked across the gutter - FIXED, UNVERIFIED (§30a).**

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, gutter between. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + 2) / 64) * 64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position).

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**⚠ THE TOPOLOGICAL TRICK DOES NOT GENERALISE TO UTILITY NETWORKS** (§30). `RegionLink` is read by the region graph and NOTHING else. Every power/pipe system builds its graph from raw CELL ADJACENCY and never consults regions. Bands are 128-256 cells apart, so no arithmetic fix exists - edges must be ADDED to each system's own builder.

**⚠ THE GUTTER IS UNBUILDABLE BY CONSTRUCTION.** `CarveGutters` writes `AB_OpenAir`, whose TerrainDef declares **no affordances at all**, while every building inherits `terrainAffordanceNeeded` Light from `BuildingBase`. Combined with every net builder stepping ONE cardinal cell, **no cell-adjacency net can cross a band unaided** - which is why §30 needs risers, and why the only vanilla power defect was the RADIUS search, not the flood fill.

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** Path grid is IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH dimensions is distorted - a bug class that cannot appear on a square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, eight shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a fraction of `Size.z` | river/lake centre; VEE Crater jitter | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient on map centre | coastline (§6e); VEE LoneIsland and Crater | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); GL landform grids (§22); **Rimefeller oil (§30e)** | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge; river WIDTH | re-base onto the cell's band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window and reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar** | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), GL roof sweep | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |
| **Foreign absolute writes** (§22) | GL landform output lands in band 0 | ORDER, not arithmetic |
| **Radius search wider than the gutter** (§30a) | `PowerConnectionMaker` ConnectMaxDist 6 vs a 3-cell gap | clip the search rect to the cell's band |

Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all `FalloffAtAngle`).
**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical FIELD rewrite** plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for direct noise samplers.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN — budget 146,000, ladder 7 / 4 / 2

**⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT BAND HEIGHT.** The original tiers were all 64k-2 and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**.

| size | slot | gutter | gap | cost/band | playable | waste | max levels | total | % budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 3 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 1.6% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 | 77% |
| **190** | 192 | 2 | 3 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 1.0% | **4** | 145,920 | 100% |
| 254 | 256 | 2 | 3 | 65,024 | 99.2% | 0.8% | 2 | 130,048 | 89% |

**⚠ THERE IS EXACTLY ONE MAXIMALLY EFFICIENT HEIGHT PER 64-STEP, SO ANCHORING ON ONE TIER FIXES THE WHOLE LADDER.** Efficient heights are `slot - 2`: **62, 126, 190, 254, 318, 382** - spaced exactly 64 apart. There is nothing efficient BETWEEN them, only heights paying for a slot they do not fill. Keeping 190 therefore *determined* 126 and 254; it was not a free choice.

**⚠ UNIFORM GUTTER IS THE REAL WIN, AND IT IS A TESTING WIN.** Every tier is now gutter 2 / gap 3, so **gutter behaviour no longer changes with the player's size pick**. Under the old ladder a gutter-crossing bug reproduced at 126 and 190 and was GEOMETRICALLY IMPOSSIBLE at 250 (gap 7) and 300 (gap 21) - the trap §30a walked into. **Every tier can now express that bug class, so a gutter test is valid on any tier.**

**⚠ WHAT WAS GIVEN UP, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A BUG.**
- **250 and 300 were vanilla's Medium and Large EXACTLY.** Players recognise those numbers; 254 and 318 are not in vanilla's list. That parity is the one real loss.
- **254 is otherwise a strict upgrade on 250** - 1.6% more cells per band buys playable 97.7% -> 99.2%, gutter 6 -> 2.
- **⚠ 318 IS BLOCKED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT PREFERENCE.** 2 x 101,760 = **203,520**, above even the old 192,000. **A second efficient size above 190 cannot exist while the budget goes down.** Raising the budget to ~204,000 is the only way to have it.
- **⚠ 62 IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT.** Efficient (slot 64, gutter 2) but 3,844 playable cells - 11% of a 190 band - and `SeamMarginFor` already takes 13% of it. **126 ALREADY produced "could not find cell to generate at" from two scatterers**, which is why that margin became derived rather than a flat 10. Half of 126 should starve generation. Do not add without measuring scatterer failures.
- **⚠ THE WIDE GUTTER WAS GENUINE SAFETY AND IS NOW GONE.** §14's "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" still holds; at gap 3 **every tier is inside the reach of a foreign radius helper**. Ours is clamped (§30a); a foreign one is not. **This is where that will show up.**

**⚠ THE BUDGET CUT, AND WHAT IT IS NOT BASED ON.** 146,000 is set by 4 x 190 = 145,920. Down from 192,000 (-24%), a figure that was itself dictated by the heaviest tier on the list - and 300 was **never generated once**. Three lines of evidence:
1. **192,000 exceeded every map vanilla ships** - 2.13x vanilla Large (90,000), 1.20x vanilla's 400x400 (160,000), already the option players are warned off. 146,000 is 1.62x Large, 0.91x that 400x400.
2. **⚠ GENERATION COST TRACKS BAND SIZE, NOT TOTAL CELLS, SO THE BUDGET GOVERNED THE WRONG AXIS.** #238 at 5 x 190 = 182,400 cells took **8.3 s**; #236 at 3 x 250 = 192,000 cells took **12.4 s**. Five percent more cells, forty-nine percent more time, because FillRock is superlinear in BAND size. Removing 250 and 300 removes the slowest generation cases outright.
3. The ceiling was only reachable by the two worst tiers; 126 never came within 41% of it.

**⚠ NOT BASED ON MEASURED FRAMERATE.** §10: the 59.6 fps benchmark measures steady state while our cost lives in section-regeneration BURSTS, never profiled. If burst cost is ever measured, revisit whether even 146,000 is right.

**⚠ COST SPREAD WAS INVERTED AND NOW IS NOT.** Old ladder ran 112,896 to 192,000 (1.70x) with the SEVEN-level tier cheapest and the TWO-level tier dearest - nobody guesses that. Now 1.29x, so the size pick is about **shape, not speed**.

**⚠ 200 IS STILL THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID** - slot 256, gutter 56, 21.9% wasted. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH.**
**Old saves are safe** - `bandHeight` is scribed, `SlotFor` is generic arithmetic, and `Sizes` is consulted only by the chooser, `Clamp` and `PlannedSize`, never on the load path. **250 and 300 colonies load and play normally.**
**⚠ THE PLAN PERSISTS BETWEEN COLONIES AND SILENTLY CONSTRAINS THE SIZE.** Read the PLAN line before believing any size test.
**⚠ Own the widget, do not patch the data.** Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly. **The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`.** The bottom strip is a fixed 240f with `InitialSize +288f`; three tiers simply leave slack, so neither needed changing.

# 3-5. MOVEMENT, ORDERING, DESCENT
**Cross-band movement** segmented at ONE interception; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop UNTESTED IN PLAY.**
**Group ordering:** the drag line runs through the GUTTER; the odd/even signature is the proof.
**⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `TryResolveVisibleBelow`.** TEN systems share it. **NINE appearances of the single-step bug.** **`TryResolveVisibleFrom` is THE gate.**
**⚠ AND THE GATE ANSWERS TWO QUESTIONS, NOT ONE** (§27).
**⚠ §29 ADDS A SECOND, RENDERING-ONLY DESCENT BESIDE IT - NOT A WIDENING OF IT.**

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION
Despeckle, central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** (#237): surface 12,723 plants; +3 **37**.
**⚠ THE SKY BAND'S OWN MASS IS `AB_MountainTop` TERRAIN AND NOTHING ELSE IDENTIFIES IT.**
**Snow-holding decides where snow fades.**

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` ports vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Confirmed five times.
**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS HANDLED** - `FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE. Preserve that.
**⚠ THREE DIFFERENT THINGS ARE ALL CALLED "MASS"** (undug edifice / sky terrain / mined leave-terrain).
**⚠ AND THE MASS FILL IS EMITTED FROM THREE PLACES** (§28).
**⚠ THE CAP IS SINGLE-STEP.** **⚠ VISIBILITY IS DECIDED ENTIRELY BY `ABBands.ShowsBelow(terrain)`.**
**⚠ A SMOOTHING KERNEL IS A SECOND CONSUMER OF THAT SAME RULE** (§27).
**⚠ AND A `dontRender` VIEWING CELL MEANS OUR FILL IS THE ONLY BACKDROP** (§28b).
**⚠ EVERY FOREIGN NETWORK SHIPS ITS OWN `SectionLayer`, AND NONE ARE MIRRORED** (§30f). DBH six, Rimatomics five, Rimefeller three, VEF one. No shared funnel.

# 6b-6g. WATER, PREVIEW, COASTS, SNOW, SHRINK
**Water** is TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE. **⚠ ALL THREE INERT UNDER GL** (§22).
**⚠ 6d-CLAMP:** `Clamp()` returns the largest offered size ≤ input; Map Preview passes VANILLA's size. **Fix: `PlannedSize`.** ⚠ Still live under the new ladder: vanilla's default 250 is no longer offered, so `Clamp(250)` now returns **190**.
**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** **Do not "simplify" `Active`.**
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong.
**6f. Below-snow:** geometry built ONCE - **never `ClearSubMeshes(All)` here**.
**Depth shrink (UNVERIFIED):** **⚠ the atlas trap**; **⚠ natural rock excluded BY DEF, not by link type**.
**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add as polish.**

# 7-8a. CHARACTER, CAMERA
Ore `x(1+0.45*(depth-1))` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`. **⚠ The snow line never worked.**
**The camera clamp and level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`.**
**New-game anchor:** only `StartedNewGame` runs after vanilla's own camera jump.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
Prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, `SCOPING:`, two censuses, the bisect state. Has voided or explained EIGHT comparisons. **⚠ THE WATER REPORT DOES NOT AND SHOULD.**

## 9b. ⚠ "COST IS DESTRUCTION NOT GENERATION" - NO LONGER TRUE. A historical record of a fixed problem.

## 9c-9f. Measured cost curve, twelve tiles
**⚠ EVERY ROW BELOW USED THE OLD LADDER.** 5x190 and 3x250 are no longer offered plans; kept because the per-band timings still hold.

| run | plan | tile | gensteps | carve | total | destroyed | suppressed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #231 | 7x126 | Flat TropSwamp | 3,836 | 1,580 | ~5.7 s | 4,575 | 1,627 |
| #236 | 3x250 | SmallHills | 5,001 | **7,118** | ~12.4 s | 15,611 | 7,272 |
| #237 | 5x190 | Mountainous | 4,529 | 2,201 | ~6.9 s | 7,497 | 85,304 |
| #238 | 5x190 | SmallHills | 3,389 | 4,718 | ~8.3 s | 16,100 | 11,175 |
| #239 | 5x190 | Mountainous Desert | 2,217 | 2,357 | **~4.7 s** | 7,906 | 76,702 |
| #248 | 5x190 | Flat Tundra | 2,108 | 3,282 | ~5.4 s | 12,103 | 5,689 |
| #254 | 5x190 | Flat Desert | 2,133 | 3,033 | ~5.2 s | 12,920 | 5,889 |
| #255 | 5x190 | Mountainous Boreal | 2,404 | **1,743** | ~4.1 s | 5,883 | **94,282** |
| #257 | 5x190 | Mountainous Boreal | 2,326 | 2,839 | ~5.2 s | 11,021 | 81,984 |

**⚠ FillRock is SUPERLINEAR in band size:** 190 -> 36,480 cells -> ~960-2,385 ms; 250 -> 64,000 -> 4,254 ms. **1.75x cells, 2.87x time.** This is the measurement that killed the 250 tier.
**⚠ HILLINESS DECIDES THE BILL, AND THE MOUNTAINOUS EXTREME IS THE CHEAPEST.** **⚠ THE `Caves` MUTATOR COSTS ~1.1-1.2 s.** **⚠ AND HILLINESS ALSO DECIDES WHETHER A RENDERING TEST IS VALID AT ALL.**
**⚠ 254 HAS NEVER BEEN GENERATED.** Extrapolating from 250 it should be the slowest offered tier; it is the one to profile first.

## 9g. ⚠ RE-RANKED ON EVIDENCE
1. **Basement rock suppression** - ~1.0-4.3 s, tile-independent. **Item 1.**
2. `GenStep_Plants` traversal scoping - 0.06-2.3 s. **Demoted.**
3. `GenStep_RockChunks`. 4. Scattered ruins. 5. Perlin precompute.

# 10-12. PERF AND DIAGNOSTICS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING** - cost is in section-regeneration BURSTS, which is also why the §2 budget rests on generation time rather than fps.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST across runs.** STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always strips its LAST entry. n=13.** Pad with a DISTINCT throwaway.
**⚠ THE AUTO-PROMPT IS EDGE-TRIGGERED, SO CHECK THE COUNT, NOT THE TEXT.**
**⚠ OUR OWN PROFILE AND BISECT LINES ARRIVE AS `warning` ROWS ATTRIBUTED TO US.**
**⚠ Debug actions are `AllowedGameStates.PlayingOnMap`.**
**⚠ AUDIT A DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN FILTERS BEFORE TRUSTING A NEGATIVE.**
**⚠ A GUARD SWITCH WITH NO CALL SITE IS NOISE.** Add one in the same commit as its guard - `Utilities` was added with §30a.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **VERIFY THE NEW LADDER.** Generate at each of 126/190/254, confirm the PLAN line, the chooser, and that a 250 or 300 save still loads.
2. **PROFILE 254** - never generated; expected to be the slowest offered tier.
3. **VERIFY §30a** at any tier (all are gap 3 now): conduit near a band's top edge, appliance just across the seam above, must NOT power up.
4. **BUILD §30b-e** - (b) power riser, (c) VEF postfix, (d) Dubwise merger, (e) Rimefeller band-local oil. Art first.
5. **VERIFY §25 on the reporter's save.**
6. **Basement rock suppression** (§9g item 1).
7. §18 audit; VEE compat; GL roof fix; reroll grid; depth shrink; camera anchor; preview at 254.
8. Stamp TILE/PLAN into the water report.
9. **Never exercised:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING/wormholes, cavern basement.
10. `ShotReport` drops target size. Biomes! at 40%. **Store page still says three levels.**
11. **§22 TABLED.** 12. **CAI 5000** (§26). 13. **§29 atlas OUTLINE queue tie.** 14. **§30g** VTE's `RoofGrid_SetRoof_Patch` vs `ABSkySync`.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. A beautiful fit is not evidence.
**⚠ ASSERTING AN INVARIANT IS NOT ESTABLISHING IT.** Carry the ANSWER, not the assumption.
**⚠ HALF-IMPOSED ORDERING IS WORSE THAN NONE.**
**⚠ FIXING A HOLE BY LOOKING SIDEWAYS WHEN THE ANSWER WAS DOWNWARD.**
**⚠ COUNT THE EMITTERS BEFORE FIXING THE LOOK.**
**⚠ CLEAR THE OTHER SUSPECT BY READING ITS DATA, NOT ITS CODE.**
**⚠ A FIX FOR MOD X CAN BE A REGRESSION FOR EVERYONE WITHOUT X.**
**⚠ REPRODUCING A SUBSYSTEM MEANS REPRODUCING ALL OF IT.**
**⚠ A COMMENT THAT JUSTIFIES SKIPPING ONE CHECK CAN BE HIDING A SECOND.**
**⚠ REUSING A PREDICATE IS REUSING ITS HIDDEN CONDITIONS.**
**⚠ AN EVENT HOOK THAT LOOKS INCREMENTAL MAY BE A FULL-MAP SWEEP ON THE LOAD PATH.**
**⚠ TWO RESOLVERS FOR ONE QUANTITY IS A BUG WITH A DELAY FUSE.**
**⚠ READ THE GUARD CLAUSES OF THE HELPER YOU ARE ABOUT TO REUSE - INCLUDING YOUR OWN.**
**⚠ ASK HOW THE SUBSYSTEM REPRESENTS THE THING, NOT WHAT THE THING IS.**
**⚠ THE USER'S REPHRASING IS DATA.** **⚠ A DIRECTIONAL WORD IN A REPORT IS A GRADIENT.**
**⚠ TWO SYMPTOMS REPORTED IN ONE BREATH ARE PROBABLY ONE BUG.**
**⚠ A SCREENSHOT CARRIES TERRAIN IDENTITY IF YOU KNOW YOUR OWN DEFS.**
**⚠ CHECK THAT YOUR CONFIGURATION CAN EXPRESS THE DIFFERENCE BEFORE RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT** - and on a banded map **the TIER is part of that configuration**. Under the old ladder a gap-3 bug could not exist at 250 or 300. **Uniform gutters remove that confound entirely, which is a testing win, not just a tidiness one.**
**⚠ NEW: A QUANTISED PARAMETER HAS FEWER LEGAL VALUES THAN IT LOOKS.** Band height appears continuous but Slot is 64-aligned, so there is exactly ONE efficient height per step (`slot - 2`: 62/126/190/254/318). Fixing any one tier fixes the entire ladder. **Before offering a "range" of options, enumerate what the quantisation actually permits - here it was five values across the whole playable span, not a spectrum.**
**⚠ NEW: A BUDGET SET BY THE HEAVIEST OPTION IS PAID BY EVERY USER.** 192,000 existed to make 250x3 and 300x2 land exactly, so the ceiling everyone carried was dictated by two tiers - one of which had **never been generated once**. **Check which option SETS a limit, and whether that option has ever been exercised.**
**⚠ NEW: A COST MODEL CAN GOVERN THE WRONG AXIS AND STILL LOOK CORRECT.** The cell budget correctly models pathfinding (IJobParallelFor over every cell) and says nothing about generation, which is superlinear in BAND size: 3x250 is 5% more cells than 5x190 and 49% more time. **When one number gates a choice, name which cost it models and check whether the cost users actually feel is the same one.**
**⚠ NEW: IF THE CHEAPEST OPTION LOOKS LIKE THE MOST EXPENSIVE, THE UI IS LYING.** The old ladder's SEVEN-level tier cost 112,896 and its TWO-level tier cost 192,000. **Keeping options within ~30% of each other lets the control be about shape rather than speed.**
**⚠ A CENSUS BEATS A MAGNITUDE.** **⚠ n=2 IS NOT A PATTERN, AND NEITHER IS n=4.**
**⚠ TILE-INDEPENDENT WINS BEAT TILE-DEPENDENT ONES.** **⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed.**
**⚠ A FIX CAN BE CHEAPER THAN THE BUG.** **⚠ WHEN A NEW RULE IS THE DUAL OF AN EXISTING ONE, SAY SO IN THE CODE.**
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM SET IS ITSELF EVIDENCE** - but a symptom pair does not pick between two mechanisms that both explain it.
**⚠ N MODS CAN BE FEWER THAN N PROBLEMS - COUNT THE CODEBASES, NOT THE MODS** (§30). Six mods, two patch families. **The mod list is a marketing artifact, not an architecture.**
**⚠ A DEPENDENCY LIST NAMES THE REAL PATCH TARGET.** **⚠ GATE AGAINST THE HOST MOD'S OWN UNLOCK, `MayRequire` INCLUDED.** **⚠ A MOD CAN HAVE A RESEARCH SYSTEM THAT IS NOT `ResearchProjectDef`.** **⚠ AN ENUM IS A CAPABILITY LIST, NOT A CONTENT LIST.**
**⚠ TWO CALL SITES OF ONE CONSTANT CAN NEED TWO DIFFERENT FIXES** (§30a). Filtering an enumeration is lossless when its caller takes everything; filtering a nearest-wins SEARCH is not. **Ask whether the caller has best-of semantics before suppressing a result.**
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.** **⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.** **⚠ A RULE ENFORCED BY GREPPING A SYNTAX ONLY CATCHES THAT SYNTAX.** **⚠ A DESIGN CHOICE RECORDED WITHOUT ITS COST WILL BE READ AS FREE.** **⚠ THE REAL CONFLICT IS USUALLY A REPLACEMENT, NOT A COLLISION.** **⚠ AND THE BUG AFTER THAT IS USUALLY A COLLABORATION.**
**⚠ CHECK WHETHER IT IS ALREADY BUILT BEFORE BUILDING IT.** **⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.**
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** **⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** **⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth.** **⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing.** **⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** **⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** **⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.** **⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return.** **⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.** **⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods.**
**Patching.** Re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the PRODUCER, not the store. Own the widget. Never put a foreign type in a patch signature. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **Prefix state is released in a Finalizer.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing it.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map.** **Read the LIVE def field, never a baked copy.** **Prefer "detect, then redo" over "always redo"** (§30a).
**Engine facts.** `holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE; `SnowGrid.CanHaveSnow` rejects on EITHER a `holdSnowOrSand=false` terrain OR a Full-fillage edifice. `SectionLayer_Snow` builds ONE nine-vertex-per-cell grid and rewrites only COLOURS. `TerrainDefGenerator_Stone` sets `edgeType = FadeRough` on `_Rough`, `_RoughHewn` AND `_Smooth`. A `TerrainHard` shader IGNORES vertex alpha; set `renderQueue` AFTER shader assignment. **Draw order between terrain materials is render QUEUE, NOT altitude or submission order.** A `dontRender` terrain makes vanilla's terrain layer emit only a ShadowMask. `Banded` is FALSE for all of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses auto-discovered on EVERY map. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread - generation latches must be `[ThreadStatic]`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. `CameraJumper.TryJump` and `MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` return silently unless `ProgramState == Playing`. Humanlikes past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED (~40x cheaper).** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws but always runs FINALIZERS; a prefix returning false skips the original but POSTFIXES STILL RUN. **`FogGrid` is a `NativeBitArray` in 1.6.** `WaterInfo.GetWaterMovement` indexes `x * map.Size.z + z`. TileMutatorDefs compete within a `categories` entry. `ThingDef.graphic` is baked at PostLoad; `graphicData.Graphic` is lazily rebuilt. `subGraphic.MatSingle` of a linked graphic is the WHOLE atlas sheet. **Vanilla rock links with `MapEdge`, so off-map counts as LINKED.** `Building.SpawnSetup` registers with the edifice grid unconditionally. `Map.FinalizeInit` calls `MapComponentUtility.FinalizeInit` LAST. `Building_Door.DrawMovers` draws the graphic TWICE. **`Graphic_Multi.Init` falls back to `_east` with `westFlipped` when `_west` is absent (and `_north` to `_south`), so a rotatable building needs only north/east/south.**
